newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dollar treads water as activity dwindles.
newsitem.headline: Dollar treads water as activity dwindles.

text.p: The dollar was fractionally off its opening levels but remained well bid on the dip in late Monday morning trade as activity dwindled due to a dearth of new leads and holidays in Tokyo and London.
Dealers said the dollar maintained a positive undertone but its upside was being capped by offers from interbank speculators seeking to take profit.
"There's a lot of technical selling at the top. And the interbank players are accumulating orders there to take profit on longs they built this morning," a European bank dealer said.
He said there were interbank offers near 1.7300 marks and 126.80 yen and selling interest from U.S. hedge funds around 1.7310/20 marks.
"On the downside, if we trade below 1.7220 marks, the market could get very nervous again," he said, adding, however, that the dollar looked supported around 1.7250 marks for the day.
The market showed little immediate reaction to German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's statement that Europe's single currency, the euro, would be introduced on schedule.
"The euro will come, will be brought about no matter what you may be reading and within the timeframe that we have agreed upon," Kohl told a news conference during an official visit to Australia.

Dealers said dollar/mark was also supported by the strong tone in sterling/mark as players focused on Wednesday's meeting between Bank of England governor Eddie George and new Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown.
"We could see some more advances in sterling today. The London futures market has priced in a 50 basis point rate hike so far," the dealer said.
"The market is looking to sell sterling/mark near 2.8100 but they're very quick to buy on any dips," he added.
